key_insight: A transformer-based decoder can learn a sharp lower bound on quantum error-correction loss via coherent information, enabling accurate threshold estimation for surface-code noise.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical ML pathway to design and evaluate quantum decoders that improve logical error suppression and help identify operating regimes where QEC remains reliable.
method: Train a transformer with maximum-likelihood decoding objectives to estimate coherent information.
Evaluate on the surface code under code-capacity, phenomenological, and circuit-level noise.
Use confidence-based soft post-selection over MLD cosets to filter uncertain outputs.
evidence_signal: The model accurately predicts coherent information, produces threshold estimates close to theory, and outperforms minimum-weight perfect matching in logical error rate on the tested noise models.
watch_item: Performance and post-selection behavior may depend on noise-model fidelity and the availability of representative training data, so deployment on hardware requires careful calibration.
paper_title: Machine Learning Optimal Quantum Error Correction Thresholds
